survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a framework for the PISA-VET assessment and contextual questionnaires, not an empirical analysis of student microdata. It therefore does not report the application of PISA/PIAAC-style sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) to produce achievement estimates. For any future empirical implementation of PISA-VET, analysts should use the official sampling/survey weights provided with the PISA-VET dataset to account for the complex multistage design (students within institutions and countries) and to support valid cross-country comparisons. Plausible values (for cognitive domains) would typically be combined using the OECD/IEA-recommended PV procedures; however, this framework chapter does not specify PV estimation or weighting variables.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD framework chapter outlines the conceptual foundations and measurement strategy for PISA-VET employability skills, rather than reporting empirical model results. It defines problem solving using PIAAC Cycle 2 “adaptive problem solving” and task performance/collaboration using the OECD Survey on Social and Emotional Skills (SSES) constructs (conscientiousness and agreeableness facets). It proposes a three-pillar assessment approach: a generic stand-alone assessment for all four employability skills (Pillar 1), an occupationally embedded component primarily for literacy and problem solving (Pillar 2), and an occupation-specific skills assessment with minimal employability-skill overlap (Pillar 3). The framework also specifies how proficiency levels may be used (e.g., reduced granularity for time-constrained generic assessments) and how contextual questionnaires should support equity/equality analyses. No sampling, scaling estimation, PV computation, or predictive modeling performance is reported in the provided text.

Consequently, there is no reported student sample size, no country-level analytic breakdown, no PV estimation method, and no missing-data handling procedure tied to an estimation model. The document focuses on measurement design (construct definitions, task formats, and questionnaire content) and therefore cannot support extraction of ML techniques or performance metrics.
